claims.text: POL-NS-01 is drafted conjunctively and the driver's side must carry all four limbs before any no-show fee is chargeable. The first limb already fails on the face of the trip record: trip_record.arrived_at is null and the trip carries no driver 'arrived' event at all, so limb (a) - a trip_record containing a driver 'arrived' event for the trip - is not satisfied. With limb (a) broken the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the question moves to the refund clauses.

Limb (b) fails on the driver's own telemetry. Across 67 fixes spanning 19:05:40 to 19:16:40 the driver's closest approach to the pickup pin was 1203.46 m (mean 1769.57 m, max 1866.98 m), against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m. The derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds. The driver was never inside the pickup geofence at any point, so limb (b) cannot be satisfied and POL-NS-02 entitles the rider to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

Limb (d) fails too, and on the platform's own reason coding. The trip was terminated by the rider at 19:16:40 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND; limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the DRIVER with RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those three codes is present and the terminating party is the rider, not the driver. A rider-cancelled trip coded RIDER_CHANGED_MIND is simply not the fact pattern POL-NS-01 was written to charge.

The waiting-period arithmetic is a complete shortfall. The effective in-geofence dwell for this STANDARD pickup is 0 seconds - derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec is 0.0 and run_count is 0 - against the 300 second minimum for the zone class, a shortfall of 300 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, so nothing about the driver's chat messages changes the arithmetic.

The only route by which the driver's time could be accumulated is closed, and I disclose why. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a qualifying traffic_advisory covers the pickup road; here the trace shows 0 in-geofence intervals, 0 runs and accumulated dwell of 0.0 seconds, so there is no second interval to add, and the advisory itself is absent. I cite that absence as an artifact of record: EV-ADVIS-00602-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. It can carry no fact; its absence is itself citable and it neither exonerates the driver nor reduces the 300 second minimum.

POL-NS-03 is a wrong-entrance clause and it cannot be turned into a driver remedy on these numbers. It requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell at a point within 400 m of the pin. The driver's minimum distance from the pin was 1203.46 m - three times the 400 m ceiling - and the distinct speeds recorded across the trace run from 12.3 to 14.8 km/h with a single 0.0 entry, so he was in motion, not holding a position. There is no wrong-face-of-the-building case here, and no platform-funded goodwill or driver compensation can arise under POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 limb (ii) points the same way. No qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the 67-fix trace, and the trip record carries no 'arrived' marker, so the waiting clock never started on any reading. On that basis the cancellation fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip falls to be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list.

The driver's first message asserted a fact the platform's own telemetry contradicts. At 19:09:40 he wrote 'you are not at the pin'. The rider track in the same trace carries 54 fixes from 19:08:40 to 19:16:37, every one of them stationary (single distinct speed 0.0) and all within 15.45 m of the pickup pin - well inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for a STANDARD pickup. The rider was at the pin for the whole window; the driver was 1.2 km away, which is why he could not see her.

The chat log shows who asked for the cancellation. The driver wrote 'battery almost 0, cannot do 22 km' and then 'can you cancel? if I cancel I kena suspend', following with 'ok fine' from the rider 30 seconds before the cancellation. That is a driver-initiated request that the rider bear the cancellation, not a rider who changed her mind about a trip the driver was ready to perform. The driver's stated distance is also uncorroborated: he says 22 km, while trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 9.0. The premise of a chargeable rider no-show under POL-NS-01 is absent from the record.

Driver compensation is conditional, not automatic. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the cancellation fee only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it'. Limb (a), limb (b), limb (c) and limb (d) of POL-NS-01 all fail on this record and POL-NS-06 independently displaces the fee, so no compensation is payable to the driver and no anti-farming escalation under POL-NS-07 or POL-NS-09(d) is engaged.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged, so this dispute can and should be decided on the merits rather than held. There is no direct conflict between admissible artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence - the trip record and the GPS trace agree that the driver never arrived - and the two citable counterparty fields are both zero: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) pushes the case below the 0.70 floor.

The money at stake is a single line and the remedy is arithmetic. The fare breakdown shows one charged item: cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00, with base_fare 0.00, distance_fare 0.00, time_fare 0.00 and platform_fee 0.00; payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. POL-NS-06 directs the refund of the cancellation-fee line only, and the 4.00 figure reconciles with the fee_schedule for a STANDARD zone on a RYDE_X vehicle tier (4.00 on both dimensions, so the greater-of rule produces 4.00). The rider's full refund is therefore SGD 4.00.

claims.text: I do not assert the anchor charge, and I say so plainly rather than stretch the record. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all — arrived_at and started_at are both null on EV-TRIP-00602 — the driver trace yields 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius with a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds against the 300 second minimum, and the trip was terminated by the rider, not the driver, under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) therefore cannot be carried on this record, and the fee is not chargeable under that clause.

Whatever is done with the fee, its quantum is fixed and no larger sum is in issue. EV-FARE-00602 charges SGD 4.00, which is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under fee_schedule.resolution_rule, and the ledger reconciles exactly to that figure — so there is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08 and the only money at stake is the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line, not any booking, base or platform component, all of which are 0.00.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Limb (a) of that clause requires a chat message that is locating or coordinating — the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle. Across the whole waiting window the rider sent exactly one message, 'ok fine' at 19:16:10, and it is none of those things. The clause therefore never engages on the rider's own chat log, and the rider cannot be presented as a party who was actively trying to be found.

The coordination failure in this window was not the driver's. The driver sent three messages between 19:09:40 and 19:11:40, each delivered and read by the rider within roughly thirty seconds, while the rider's first and only reply came six and a half minutes later. POL-NS-04 rests on the premise that the rider was actively coordinating; on this record the party who was communicating promptly and candidly about his position and his situation was the driver, and the party who said nothing locating until the very end was the rider.

No false-arrival referral should be recorded against the driver. POL-NS-05 is triggered by an 'arrived' event whose timestamp the GPS trace contradicts; this trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all, so the false-marker limb, and with it the limb (ii) referral for recording a false-arrival event against the driver, is not engaged. The driver never claimed to have arrived even though he had every incentive to tap 'arrived' and let the clock run — the honest course, and the precise opposite of the fee-farming conduct that limb (ii)'s referral exists to catch.

ruling.explanation:
The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

Chargeability under POL-NS-01. The clause charges a no-show fee only if all four of its conditions hold, and on this record none does. (a) The trip record carries no driver 'arrived' event — trip_record.arrived_at is null and started_at is null (EV-TRIP-00602). (b) The GPS trace never places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival geofence: across 67 fixes his closest approach to the pickup pin was 1203.46 m (mean 1769.57 m), and derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 (EV-GPS-00602). (c) Effective in-geofence dwell was 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum — a 300-second shortfall (EV-GPS-00602). (d) The trip was terminated by the RIDER at 19:16:40 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, not by the DRIVER under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT (EV-TRIP-00602). Both advocates' citations of POL-NS-01 on limbs (a), (b) and (d) are accepted, and the rider's limb (c)/POL-NS-06 arithmetic is accepted. With POL-NS-01 unsatisfied, POL-NS-02 independently entitles the rider to a full refund (no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before cancellation), and POL-NS-06 confirms it.

Amount. The only money in issue is the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 on EV-FARE-00602; base, distance, time and platform components are all 0.00, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The figure reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule for a STANDARD zone (SGD 4.00) on a RYDE_X tier (SGD 4.00): the greater of the two is SGD 4.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare-integrity defect and no larger sum is at stake. Full refund of SGD 4.00 is therefore the whole remedy.

Driver compensation. POL-NS-07 pays 80% of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. It is not satisfied and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so no compensation is payable and the anti-farming check is never reached. POL-NS-03 cannot supply a remedy either: it requires the driver to have held position within 400 m of the pin, and his minimum distance was 1203.46 m, three times that ceiling.

False-arrival referral — not recorded. POL-NS-05 is triggered by an 'arrived' event that the GPS trace contradicts, and its limb (ii) referral records a FALSE arrival marker against the driver. This trip record carries no arrival marker at all, so there is no false event to record; the driver's claim on this point is accepted and the rider's request for a false-arrival referral is declined. No other referral clause fires — POL-NS-07 anti-farming does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against completed_trips_30d 110), so referrals is empty.

Points that do not move the outcome. The driver's observation that he messaged promptly while the rider's only reply came six minutes later is accurate as far as it goes, but fault allocation of that kind belongs to POL-NS-03, which does not apply; a prompt driver cannot revive a fee the anchor clause does not authorise. The driver's point that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider is accepted but immaterial — the refund rests on POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, not POL-NS-04. The driver's two chat assertions ('you are not at the pin'; 'cannot do 22 km') are contradicted by the platform's own telemetry: the rider's device sat stationary within 15.45 m of the pin across 54 fixes from 19:08:40 to 19:16:37, and trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 9.0, not 22 km. The MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00602-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload) can carry no fact; its absence does not reduce the 300-second minimum and does not excuse the shortfall, and it is named here per POL-GEN-02(3).

Escalation. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged: the deciding facts come from artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no policy-level impairment, the trip record and GPS trace agree rather than contradict, confidence is above the 0.70 floor, and no repeat-dipute or abuse counter is met. The case is decided on the merits.

For the reviewer's awareness only (not a clause-mandated referral): the driver's chat asked the rider to cancel because cancelling himself risked a suspension, and the ride was then cancelled under RIDER_CHANGED_MIND. That request, and the driver's uncorroborated distance claim, may be of interest to the platform's conduct processes, but no clause in this category produces an instruction to act on it.

Confidence. The deciding facts — non-arrival, zero qualifying dwell, the rider's presence, and the SGD 4.00 quantum — are carried by EV-GPS-00602, EV-TRIP-00602 and EV-FARE-00602, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the ruling rests at 0.95.

The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) pushes the case below the 0.70 floor.

The money at stake is a single line and the remedy is arithmetic. The fare breakdown shows one charged item: cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00, with base_fare 0.00, distance_fare 0.00, time_fare 0.00 and platform_fee 0.00; payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. POL-NS-06 directs the refund of the cancellation-fee line only, and the 4.00 figure reconciles with the fee_schedule for a STANDARD zone on a RYDE_X vehicle tier (4.00 on both dimensions, so the greater-of rule produces 4.00). The rider's full refund is therefore SGD 4.00.

I do not assert the anchor charge, and I say so plainly rather than stretch the record. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all — arrived_at and started_at are both null on EV-TRIP-00602 — the driver trace yields 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius with a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds against the 300 second minimum, and the trip was terminated by the rider, not the driver, under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) therefore cannot be carried on this record, and the fee is not chargeable under that clause.

Whatever is done with the fee, its quantum is fixed and no larger sum is in issue. EV-FARE-00602 charges SGD 4.00, which is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under fee_schedule.resolution_rule, and the ledger reconciles exactly to that figure — so there is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08 and the only money at stake is the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line, not any booking, base or platform component, all of which are 0.00.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Limb (a) of that clause requires a chat message that is locating or coordinating — the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle. Across the whole waiting window the rider sent exactly one message, 'ok fine' at 19:16:10, and it is none of those things. The clause therefore never engages on the rider's own chat log, and the rider cannot be presented as a party who was actively trying to be found.

The coordination failure in this window was not the driver's. The driver sent three messages between 19:09:40 and 19:11:40, each delivered and read by the rider within roughly thirty seconds, while the rider's first and only reply came six and a half minutes later. POL-NS-04 rests on the premise that the rider was actively coordinating; on this record the party who was communicating promptly and candidly about his position and his situation was the driver, and the party who said nothing locating until the very end was the rider.

No false-arrival referral should be recorded against the driver. POL-NS-05 is triggered by an 'arrived' event whose timestamp the GPS trace contradicts; this trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all, so the false-marker limb, and with it the limb (ii) referral for recording a false-arrival event against the driver, is not engaged. The driver never claimed to have arrived even though he had every incentive to tap 'arrived' and let the clock run — the honest course, and the precise opposite of the fee-farming conduct that limb (ii)'s referral exists to catch.
